act: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5 (Editor's Draft, 13 April 2026)

en.title: CSS Cascade 5: the Layer Ordering example gives two different orders when both media queries match
en.summary: Example #example-87e2d331 in §6.4.3 says that when the width query matches, layout comes first, and that when the colour-scheme query matches, theme comes first. When both match, the two sentences give different orders. The rule of §6.4.3 (layers sort by first declaration) gives layout first; only the second sentence is wrong. The 2022 snapshot of the specification (13 January 2022) has the same example.
en.impact: A wide viewport with a dark colour-scheme preference and the same property in both layers: by the rule the later layer, theme, wins; by the second sentence of the example layout wins.
en.correction: Make the second sentence apply only when the width query does not match: “Otherwise, theme will come first in the layer order.”

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: Cascade layers are sorted by the order in which they first are declared, with nested layers grouped within their parent layer.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: If the first media-query matches based on viewport dimensions, then the layout layer will come first in the layer order.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: If the color-scheme preference query matches, or if neither condition is true, then theme will come first in the layer order.
